subject: Tufts University Institutional Zoning District
overview: The Community Development Board and city staff held an information session to discuss the creation of a dedicated institutional zoning district for the Tufts University campus. The board reviewed current zoning gaps, the impact of the Dover Amendment on municipal authority, and strategies for regulating building heights and setbacks near residential neighborhoods.

items.title: Zoning Project Timeline and Framework
items.summary: Staff outlined the 2025 zoning process, explaining how residential and commercial frameworks from the comprehensive plan will be translated into new zoning ordinances.

items.title: Proposed Institutional District Boundaries
items.summary: Presenters displayed a proposed boundary map for the Medford portion of the Tufts campus and solicited public input on whether specific industrial and corridor areas should be included in the district.

items.title: Analysis of Current Dimensional Standards
items.summary: Staff explained that because Medford lacks a dedicated campus district, current zoning allows heights up to 15 stories for certain educational uses, a loophole the new district aims to close.

items.title: Public Comment on Building Scale and Use
items.summary: Residents expressed concerns about high-rise dormitories on the hillside, advocating for lower height limits, stepped-down building scales, and protection of existing green spaces like Stearns Field.

items.title: Dover Amendment Limitations and Authority
items.summary: Staff clarified that while the state's Dover Amendment exempts educational uses from certain zoning restrictions, the city retains the right to enforce reasonable dimensional standards such as setbacks and heights.

items.title: Somerville Special District Model Review
items.summary: The board reviewed Somerville's Tufts University zoning model, which utilizes a height map with concentric bands that decrease building height limits as they approach residential property lines.

items.title: Future Zoning Drafts and Scheduling
items.summary: The committee scheduled upcoming discussions for May 14 and May 28, noting that a GIS mapping tool will soon be released to help residents track property ownership and proposed changes.
